review: Prism using Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5, followed by primary and independent internal source adjudication
resolution: Three findings refuted from actual source; one intentional strict-sync filesystem/platform limitation retained. No source changes after Prism, so no unchanged repeat review.

findings.reason: Application.Open installs a nonnil lifetime before registration and forbids ID reuse. CloseWindow cancels the lifetime but never deletes it; only windows and dirty state are removed. CheckCloseWindow rechecks under app.mu, returning ErrWindowClosed/ErrClosed after concurrent closure.

Strict post-rename directory synchronization is an intentional contract. Failure returns Written=true and Err, withholding save acknowledgment/automatic close. Local Mac checks qualify the tested temporary volume, not other mounted/network/removable filesystems. Windows/Linux runtime behavior is deferred. Blanket EINVAL/ENOTSUP/EPERM suppression would change durability semantics and may hide genuine failures; any best-effort policy requires explicit semantics and target tests.

Application.Do is synchronous: it locks the serialized owner and invokes fn directly in the calling test goroutine. It does not schedule work on another goroutine. These headless tests never start a native run loop; Fatal/Goexit executes the deferred owner unlock.

Every live model/session/journal/workflow/registry access in runDocumentSmoke occurs inside documentOwner/documentWait, whose callbacks execute under Do. captureDocument clones all slices; worker comparisons and final decoding use detached private snapshots. The failure injection flag is atomic. Native WindowByName and CloseReq use the synchronized backend path. The final million-component fixture passed with race detection.
